verdict.rationale: OpenClaw documents real desktop apps (macOS menu bar app with native Mac tabs, a signed Windows Hub installer, Linux companion), mobile iOS/Android 'node' apps, and a browser Control UI served by the Gateway, plus richer-than-chat capabilities (camera/device control, computer-use, screen/system access) exposed through these surfaces. However, these are framed primarily as node/pairing/control companions rather than full first-class chat clients with explicit feature-parity claims versus the core chat experience, and there's no independent hands-on confirmation of parity across all these apps. Missing for 10: explicit vendor statement of feature parity across web/desktop/mobile vs chat, independent/hands-on verification of these companion apps, and clarity that they are full chat surfaces rather than device-control add-ons.
